Job Description

Are you ready to make a real, positive impact in the lives of adults with learning disabilities? Join East Sussex County Council’s Community Learning Disability Service, where your professional expertise will help adults live independent, fulfilled lives within their communities.

We are currently recruiting for experienced and committed Social Workers who are confident working in a complex legal and safeguarding landscape. We have offices for the team based in both Hastings and Uckfield.

You'll be part of a supportive, multidisciplinary team committed to strengths-based practice and person-centred care. Whether you’re seeking to expand your skills in legal frameworks, safeguarding, or mental capacity work, or looking for a place to grow your career, East Sussex is the place to do it.

You'll be managing complex caseloads, prioritising cases with Court of Protection deadlines and safeguarding needs, and acting as Lead Enquiry Officer in Section 42 Safeguarding Enquiries under the Care Act 2014. You will apply the Mental Capacity Act (MCA) in practice and making Best Interests decisions, and will contribute to community DoL assessments and applications to the Court of Protection (s21A/s16). The role will involve working collaboratively with partner agencies, legal teams, and health professionals, as well as attending court where required and potentially applying transferable legal experience such as Mental Health Tribunals or Magistrates Court warrants.

We Are Looking For Candidates Who

Has social work qualifications and registered with the professional regulatory body
Has successfully completed Assessed and Supported Year in employment, or the equivalent if prior to 2012, (NQSW year and academic module) or equivalent
Can demonstrate knowledge of appropriate legal and policy frameworks and an awareness of current case law, that informs and mandates social work practice
Is able to demonstrate accountability and effective judgement when anticipating, identifying, assessing and managing risk, seeking support and solutions where appropriate
Has the ability to promote, develop and establish effective, collaborative partnerships and networks to promote appropriate information sharing, and utilise the expertise of external agency professionals, service users and carers
Is able to work positively with others and contribute to team working and a learning environment for self, team and colleagues
Can meet the travelling requirements of the post

Please download the Job Description and Person Specification for more information.

To apply for this role, click the apply now button to upload a CV with a Supporting Statement. Please tell us how your skills, experience, and values make you a great fit for this role and ensure your Supporting Statement clearly addresses how you meet all the criteria in the person specification.

For guidance on how to write an application see our how to apply page and our statement on the use of AI .

Interviews will be held via Microsoft Teams within 2 weeks of the closing date.

Candidates who meet certain criteria are given priority when we shortlist. See our priority status page for details.

We would really like you to choose the Learning Disability service for your next step in social work. Why join us?

A strong focus on person-centred, strengths-based social work.
Opportunities to shape decision-making in areas such as Best Interests, community Deprivation of Liberty (DoL), and the Mental Capacity Act.
The chance to work on Court of Protection (COP) applications, including Section 21A and Section 16.
Hybrid working arrangements.
A supportive team and professional development opportunities, including pathways to roles such as Best Interests Assessor (BIA) and Practice Educator Professional Standards (PEPS).

We offer a diverse range of benefits to help and support you during your employment. More information can be found on our benefits page.

For an informal discussion, email Scott Templeman, Operations Manager, scott.templeman@eastsussex.gov.uk and he will be happy to arrange a call to answer any questions.

Vocational Training through Apprenticeships is now available to our staff, ranging from entry level to degree level qualifications. You can talk to the hiring manager and the apprenticeship team about what qualifications would be relevant to you and this job role, and if it is possible to support you in apprenticeship training.

For work that makes a difference, choose East Sussex!

The Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science (CDU) Center for Accelerating Excellence in Translational Science (AXIS) has focused on eliminating health disparities in the south Los Angeles community, particularly those related to cancer, cardiometabolic diseases, and HIV/AIDS. Company Description

Anglo American Australia

In Australia, we operate five steelmaking coal mines in Queensland’s Bowen Basin, and have additional joint venture interests in manganese, as well as copper exploration projects under way in North West Queensland. Steelmaking coal is an essential ingredient in blast-furnace steel manufacture, producing steel used for critical building and infrastructure around the world. 

Job Description

We are currently seeking a highly motivated training professional competent in developing, scheduling, and delivering training and related activities and ensuring compliance with corporate and statutory requirements.

As the Training Coordinator reporting to the Training Superintendent, your duties include:

Validating training and assessment compliance of all Coal Mine workers at Capcoal.
Maintaining compliance of the Site Induction and delivering Inductions to Employees and Contractors
Assist in Coaching/Mentoring employees and contractors in developing skill/experience that’s relevant to work requirements to ensure all Coal Mine workers at Capcoal are trained, competent and authorised as per the Capcoal Mine Training and Competence Scheme.
Enforcing the requirements of the Coal Mine Training and Competence Scheme and Training Process.
Undertaking reviews on training performance, for continuous improvement of training procedures and processes.
Knowledge of Learning Management Systems in maintaining site compliance and provision of governance to ensure the systems are applied consistently across the mine.
Engage with key stakeholders in all aspects of training to assist in the delivery of the business plan.
Demonstrate being a ‘Safety Leader’ and encourage people to be Safe at Work, engage with the workforce to improvement Safety Culture performance.

Qualifications

The key attributes contributing to your success in this role will include:

Certificate IV in Training and Assessment (TAE40116/22 or equivalent) or higher.
Operational experience within coal mining is preferred.
Experience using Microsoft Suite Applications including Excel and PowerPoint, and knowledge of Learning Management Systems (LMS).
Experience in driving best practise through your department and into the business; this includes the development and implementation of strategy in line with business goals.
Experience in assisting with Training departmental budget and expenditure.
Strong interpersonal and negotiation skills to influence and achieve buy in from key stakeholders.
Experience in dealing with high volume work during major works e.g. shutdowns
Ability to be adaptable in changing situations and able to step through the issue using your strong problem-solving skills.
Proficiency in managing and delivering site-based training requirements and programs.

Additional Information

Permanent, full-time position at Capcoal Mine, Middlemount QLD.
Monday to Friday site role with the potential for a 9-day fortnight
Residential, DIDO and FIFO (company funded) options
Competitive salary + 12% superannuation and annual bonus
Subsidised housing, with relocation assistance if required
Discounted gym membership
Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for employees and their family

What We Offer

When you join Anglo American, you can expect to enjoy a competitive salary and benefits package and a range of flexible work arrangements that support the balance of work, family and individual circumstances. But more than this, you’ll find yourself in an environment where the opportunities for learning and growth are second to none. From technical training to leadership programs, we bring out the best in our people. There are plenty of opportunities to move onwards and upwards too.

Who We Are

We aim to lead the industry by pursuing ever safer and more responsible ways of working, demonstrating integrity, and showing care and respect for people and the planet. That means we are constantly seeking new opportunities to mine and process our products sustainably, using less water, less energy and more precise extraction technologies.  Anglo American is a leading global mining company focused on the responsible production of copper, premium iron ore and crop nutrients – future-enabling products that are essential for decarbonising the global economy, improving living standards, and food security. Our extraordinary teams work safely and collaboratively to unlock enduring value from precious natural resources for our shareholders, for the benefit of the communities and countries in which we operate, and for society as a whole. Anglo American is re-imagining mining to improve people’s lives.

Inclusion and Diversity

Anglo American is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promoting an inclusive and diverse workplace where we value and respect every colleague for who they are and provide equality of opportunity so that everyone can fulfil their potential.

How We Are Committed To Your Safety

Nothing is more important to us than ensuring you return home safely after a day’s work. To make that happen, we have the most rigorous safety standards in the industry. Not only that, we’re also continually investing in new technologies – from drones to data analytics – that are helping to make mining safer.

With a fantastic skilled team, plus a state-of-the-art nurturing environment the residents are offered all-round support. Each young person has a bespoke care plan to ensure support and agreed areas of work to meet their education and health needs.

You’ll be a visible leader who brings a presence to the home, planning residential support worker’s shifts, leading shifts on a day to day basis, ensuring that the children are kept engaged and that their emotional and physical wellbeing is being cared for. This is a challenging role as it involves you taking the lead in a constructive and proactive way to address the problematic behaviour presented by the children, so requires resilience and self-awareness.

We Are Looking For Candidates Who

Are organised
Are self-motivated
Have communication skills
Experienced in managing behaviour using physical restraint and knows how to guide others through intervention safely
